findings.title: OAEI 2026 Campaign: New Tracks and Evaluation Infrastructure
findings.venue: Ontology Alignment Evaluation Initiative (OAEI) / ISWC 2026 Workshop
findings.key_findings: OAEI 2026 introduces several new tracks and significant infrastructure changes: (1) Migration to MELT platform for evaluation, enabling non-Java systems. (2) New Bio-ML track with two CodaBench competitions: Subtrack 1 (Global equivalence alignment - repaired, coherence-aware P/R/F1 with reasoner-checked Global Coherence score) and Subtrack 2 (Local equivalence ranking - MRR and Hits@{1,5,10} on gold-stripped candidate pools). Bio-ML supersedes LargeBio and Phenotype tracks, matching NCIT–DOID, SNOMED–FMA, SNOMED–NCIT pairs. (3) New DISO-OAEI track for defence/intelligence/security ontologies: 8 matching tasks over 60+ curated OWL ontologies, consensus alignments from multiple matchers, silver-standard reference from manual curation. (4) New Beyond Equivalence track for complex correspondences. (5) Digital Humanities and Archaeology multilingual tracks. (6) TD→KG track with prizes from SIRIUS and IBM Research. Evaluation closes Sept 30, 2026; results at OM Workshop collocated with ISWC 2026 in Bari.

findings.title: LogMap-LLM: Large Language Models as Oracles for Ontology Alignment (EACL 2026)
findings.key_findings: LogMap-LLM integrates LLMs as targeted Oracles only for uncertain mappings (M_ask subset) rather than full alignment. Uses LogMap as baseline with 6 prompt templates and 5 LLMs (GPT-4o-mini, Gemini Flash 2.0/2.5, Mistral, Llama, Qwen). Achieved top-2 overall rank in OAEI 2025 Bio-ML track. Evaluated diagnostic capabilities via Sensitivity, Specificity, Youden's Index (YI) on M_ask. Best LLM Oracle (Gemini Flash 2.5 with extended context + synonyms NLF prompts) achieved average YI > 0.5 vs LogMap's ~0. Statistical tests show LogMap+Or_GF2.5 significantly outperforms LogMap (p=0.02) and simulated Oracles up to 20% error. Code at github.com/city-artificial-intelligence/logmap-llm and github.com/city-artificial-intelligence/rai-ukraine-kga-llm.

findings.title: KROMA: Ontology Matching with Knowledge Retrieval and Large Language Models
findings.key_findings: KROMA introduces bisimilarity-based concept matching and lightweight ontology refinement to prune candidates and reduce LLM calls. Formalizes semantic equivalence as bisimilar equivalence relation with minimality/uniqueness guarantees on concept graphs. Supports both offline (cold-start) and online (streaming) matching with low-polynomial algorithms. Integrates knowledge retrieval from external resources to enrich LLM prompts. Outperforms existing LLM-based methods by 10.95% average F1; knowledge retrieval improves accuracy by 6.65%, refinement by 2.68%. Tested on 6 OAEI benchmarks. Uses Llama-3.1-70B; code at github.com/lamng3/kroma.

findings.title: GenOM: Ontology Matching with Description Generation and Large Language Models
findings.venue: World Wide Web Journal / ISWC 2025 OM Workshop
findings.key_findings: GenOM generates semantically enriched textual definitions for each concept using LLMs (Qwen2.5-7B/14B/32B, Llama3-8B), embeds them for candidate retrieval, then applies LLM-based mapping judgement + exact matching for precision. Achieves competitive performance on 5 OAEI Bio-ML tasks (SNOMED-CT, NCIT, FMA, ORDO, DOID, OMIM), surpassing traditional and LLM-based baselines. Novel evaluation methodology for LLM-generated definitions: lexical metrics + LLM-as-a-judge (discriminative 1-5, correctness 1-5). Ablation confirms semantic enrichment and few-shot prompting are critical. 8% recall improvement over BERTMapLt, 24% over LogMapLt. Code at github.com/AlanS87/genom-pipeline.

findings.title: MILA: Ontology Matching with LLMs and Prioritized Depth-First Search
findings.key_findings: MILA embeds retrieve-identify-prompt pipeline within Prioritized Depth-First Search (PDFS) strategy. Alternates search between source/target ontologies via search tree; uses dual retrievers (SBERT) to prioritize successors; identifies high-confidence bidirectional correspondences via objective function; only prompts LLM for borderline cases. Achieved highest F-measure in 4/5 unsupervised OAEI 2023/2024 biomedical tasks, outperforming state-of-the-art by up to 17%. Performs comparably to supervised systems. Task-agnostic, stable across settings, significantly reduces LLM requests. No fine-tuning or domain-specific heuristics needed. Code at github.com/mariatab/MILA.

findings.title: OAEI-LLM-T: TBox Benchmark for LLM Hallucinations in Ontology Matching
findings.key_findings: First benchmark dataset for LLM hallucinations in TBox (class/property) ontology matching. Evolves 7 OAEI schema-matching datasets. Benchmarks 10 LLMs on OM tasks. Classifies hallucinations into 2 primary categories and 6 sub-categories (missing mappings, incorrect mappings, align-up/down, disputed). Enables LLM leaderboard for OM tasks and fine-tuning dataset for OM-specific LLM optimization. Dataset and code at github.com/qzc438-research/ontology-hallucination. Baseline Agent-OM at github.com/qzc438/ontology-llm. Extends OAEI-LLM (2024) proposal.

findings.title: Crowd-OM: Crowdsourcing for Ontology Matching Validation
findings.key_findings: Addresses validation bottleneck for LLM-based OM systems that produce many disputed mappings not in ground-truth references. Introduces Crowd-OM system with three quality-assurance mechanisms: (1) Differential trustworthiness - seed pairs assess annotator reliability, weights expert decisions higher. (2) Coherence pre-filling - in-built reasoner pre-fills decisions from completed answers to reduce manual errors. (3) Time-dependent opinion - continuous editing mode tracks decision changes in real-time. Two-sided marketplace model (Admin, Developer, Annotator roles). Evaluated in controlled scenarios showing robustness against non-expert annotators. Extends to subsumption matching via logical extensions.

findings.title: OAEI 2025 Results and Evaluation Metrics
findings.venue: ISWC 2025 OM Workshop / DTU Orbit / INRIA HAL
findings.key_findings: OAEI 2025: 12 tracks, 20 participants. Standard metrics: Precision, Recall, F-measure (harmonic mean) for classes, properties, instances. Recall+ excludes trivial correspondences (same normalized label). Coherence checked via Pellet reasoner (conservativity/consistency violations). F0.5 and F2 measures for precision/recall weighting. Knowledge Graph track: separate P/R/F1 for classes, properties, instances. Local ranking evaluation: Hits@K and MRR for subsumption mappings. MELT framework used for evaluation (5-core CPU, 16GB RAM). OAEI 2025 results show Matcha top in Anatomy (F1=0.941), Agent-OM and LogMapLLM as new high-performing LLM-based entrants.

findings.title: DISO-OAEI: Defence Intelligence Security Ontology Alignment Track
findings.key_findings: New OAEI 2026 track for defence/national security. 60+ public OWL ontologies documented across 13 clusters (cyber-security 15, mid-level 12, smart environments 8, upper-level 8, etc.). 1,653 ontology pairs aligned; consensus alignments from multiple state-of-the-art matchers via family-based voting; silver-standard from manual curation of consensus + unique mappings. Silver-standard fixed for logical errors and incoherent mappings. 8 matching tasks. DISO ecosystem: diso collection, diso-mappings pipeline, diso-oaei track page. Resources on Hugging Face (OAEI-ML/diso-oaei) and Zenodo. Plans for automated benchmarking, active leaderboard, ranking task like Bio-ML.

findings.title: Stable Matching Approaches in Ontology Alignment
findings.key_findings: Gale-Shapley stable matching applied to partial graph matching in supervised learning setting. Ouali et al. (2019) used stable matching for ontology alignment quality improvement through efficient optimization. Creates faster, more robust alignment method. In 2025 surveys (Emergent Mind), stable matching referenced as foundational approach but newer LLM-based systems (MILA, KROMA, GenOM) use different strategies (PDFS, bisimulation, description generation). No major 2025-2026 publications specifically advancing stable matching for OM; field has shifted to LLM-hybrid approaches.

findings.title: Agent-OM: LLM Agents for Ontology Matching
findings.key_findings: Agent-OM framework: LLM as central "brain" with planning modules (CoT for OM decomposition), OM tools (ICL/RAG for hallucination mitigation), memory storage. Three architectures compared: LLM-Only, LLM-with-Context, Agent-OM. Agent-OM achieves considerable improvements across 3 OAEI tracks. Key insight: agents can orchestrate retrieval, matching, and validation as separate tools rather than monolithic prompting. Code at github.com/qzc438/ontology-llm (linked from OAEI-LLM-T).

findings.title: Ontology Alignment Evaluation Metrics - Current Standards
findings.key_findings: Core metrics: Precision = |M_S ∩ M_RA|/|M_S|, Recall = |M_S ∩ M_RA|/|M_RA|, F1 = 2·P·R/(P+R). Extended metrics: Recall+ (excludes trivial label-equivalent mappings). Coherence: Pellet reasoner checks for conservativity/consistency violations. Weighted F-measures: F0.5 (precision-weighted), F2 (recall-weighted). For ranking tasks (subsumption): Hits@K, MRR. For Bio-ML 2026: Global Coherence score (reasoner-checked), MRR, Hits@{1,5,10} for local ranking. For DISO: consensus alignment + silver-standard manual curation. MELT platform standardizes evaluation across tracks (5-core CPU, 16GB RAM).

summary: As of September 2026, ontology alignment has undergone a major shift toward LLM-integrated hybrid systems. The OAEI 2026 campaign introduces new tracks (Bio-ML with ML-friendly dual evaluation, DISO for defence/security, Beyond Equivalence, multilingual DH) and migrates to the MELT platform. Key systems: LogMap-LLM (EACL 2026) uses LLMs as targeted Oracles for uncertain mappings, achieving top-2 in Bio-ML 2025; KROMA (ISWC 2025) introduces bisimulation-based concept graphs with knowledge retrieval, outperforming LLM baselines by ~11%; GenOM (WWW 2026) generates LLM-enriched definitions for semantic enrichment, beating traditional and LLM baselines on Bio-ML; MILA (Information Fusion 2025) uses Prioritized Depth-First Search to minimize LLM calls, winning 4/5 unsupervised tasks. Evaluation advances: OAEI-LLM-T provides first hallucination taxonomy/benchmark for LLM-based OM; Crowd-OM (PVLDB 2027) addresses validation bottleneck via crowdsourcing with quality assurance. Stable matching remains a foundational reference but is not the focus of 2025-2026 advances. Metrics now include coherence-aware scores, ranking metrics (MRR, Hits@K), and hallucination-specific taxonomies.
